notes: Primary ask: enterprise-grade Dedicated with explicit throughput guarantees (min tokens/sec) and deterministic concurrency caps for sub-200ms p95 chat responses at 512-token context
Equinox CTO (S. Patel): 'We need predictable tail latency during market open spikes. If you can't guarantee throughput, we can't sign.'

Targets discussed: baseline 10k tokens/sec sustained, 20k tokens/sec burst for up to 10 minutes, concurrency cap 500 active sessions, P95 latency target <200ms for single-token generation on short requests
Measurement proposal from Redwood eng: 60-second sliding window for tokens/sec with 5-minute rolling aggregate for billing; separate meter for burst minutes used

Equinox pushback: sliding window too noisy for tail guarantees — asked for 'min sustained for 5 minutes' metric instead. Want explicit SLA credit formula tied to 5-min sustained throughput and p95 latency breaches

Burst policy negotiation: Equinox wants 2x burst without immediate overage fees for first 10 minutes per day, then tiered charges. Redwood proposed burst pool with pre-paid burst minutes at a discounted rate.

Concurrency enforcement: Discussed soft vs hard caps. Equinox requires hard concurrency cap per-tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor; Redwood suggested request queueing with priority lanes to preserve latency SLOs

Reserved GPU planning: initial recommendation 8x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent quantized nv24 nodes) with sharding config to hit baseline under expected mix. SE provided model footprints and sim results.

Canary and validation plan: 7-day canary with sample traffic generator (repo stub linked) — success criteria: sustained 95% of baseline throughput and zero P95 latency breaches >200ms for control workload
POC measurements: internal perf run yielded 11.3k tokens/sec sustained at 80% utilization with estimated headroom for bursts to 19k tokens/sec on additional burst nodes

Billing and penalties: Equinox wants SLA credits (service credits) calculated as percentage of monthly fee if min tokens/sec or latency SLO violated for cumulative more than 30min/month. Redwood wants cap on credits and opt-in for higher-penalty tiers.
Integrations: require KMS integration for model keys and audit log export to Equinox SIEM; data residency requirement to keep embeddings in us-east-1 only
Open questions: exact token definition for measuring (post-tokenizer vs raw bytes), network overhead allowances, multi-tenant fallback rules if dedicated pool under pressure
Next tacticals: legal to draft SLA clause with 5-minute sustained throughput metric, engineering to produce a 'burst minute' pricing appendix, schedule 1-week canary in May if procurement clears
